Report Description/// NOAA/NESDIS MPSR ISSUED FOR: GULF OF AMERICA /// POSSIBLE, UNCONFIRMED OIL WAS OBSERVED IN SATELLITE IMAGERY. REPORT DATE: 03-22-2026 REPORT TIME: 0041 UTC REGION: GULF OF AMERICA SUB REGION: N/A AREA/BLOCK: SHIP SHOAL 44 IMAGE DATE: 03-21-2026 IMAGE TIME: 2358 UTC DATA SOURCE: RADARSAT2 MODE: SCANSAR NARROW VV RESOLUTION: 50 METER LOCATION: 29°03'40" N/90°49'43" W AREA: 6.84 SQUARE KILOMETERS CONFIDENCE: HIGH REPORT MAP/GIS FILES: HTTPS://WWW.OSPO.NOAA.GOV/PRODUCTS/OCEAN/MARINEPOLLUTION/ REMARKS: POSSIBLE OIL WAS OBSERVED IN SATELLITE IMAGERY. THIS ANOMALY IS UNCONFIRMED AS OIL. THE FRAGMENTED SLICK WAS BELIEVED TO BE ASSOCIATED WITH NOAA RESPONSE LINK HOTLINE #11125. IT WAS OBSERVED NORTH OF WHISKEY ISLAND, LOUISIANA. properties.summary: Incident Type: MOBILE - NRC Report ID: 1048247 - Medium Affected: LAND - Suspected Responsible Party: SOUTHEAST BIODIESEL
properties.content:
Report Details
NRC Report ID: 1048247
Incident Time: 2013-05-24 13:10:00
Nearest City: North Charleston, SC
Location: AT BIODIESEL MANUFACTURING PLANT, IN THE AREA DESIGNATED FOR LOADING TRUCKS. 1005 KINZER STREET
Incident Type: MOBILE
Material: WASTEWATER
Medium Affected: LAND
Suspected Responsible Party: SOUTHEAST BIODIESEL
SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 32.877222, -79.969722 (Explicit)
Reported Spill Volume: 300 gallon
Report Description
****WEB REPORT**** A TANK TRUCK WAS BEING LOADED WITH USED WASH WATER. DUE TO A MECHANICAL FAILURE APPROXIMATELY 300 GALLONS OF THIS WATER WAS SPILLED ON THE GROUND. THE SPILLED WATER MADE ITS WAY ONTO AN ADJACENT CONCRETE YARD. APPROXIMATELY 50 GALLONS OF THE SPILLED WATER OVERFLOWED THROUGH A BOUNDARY FENCE TO AN ADJACENT PROPERTY LOCATED TO THE SOUTH. SITE MANAGERS ON THE ADJACENT SITE SAW THE FLOW OF WATER AND PREVENTED IT FROM ENTERING THE STORM DRAINAGE SYSTEM. A VACUUM TANKER TRUCK WAS DEPLOYED TO COLLECT THE WATER THAT HAD POOLED ON THE GROUND. THERE WAS NO OIL IN THE WATER. THE SLICK WAS LINEAR IN SHAPE, HAD A DARK AND STRONG CONTRAST TO THE SURROUNDING ENVIRONMENT, AND APPEARED TO EMANATE FROM THE ELOI BAY WITHIN THE BIRD FOOT DELTA OF THE GULF OF MEXICO. THE SLICK WAS APPROXIMATELY 0.89NM IN LENGTH, AND APPROXIMATELY 0.11NM AT THE WIDEST POINT. THERE WAS A BRIGHT RETURN WITHIN THE SLICK EXTENTS, WHICH ARE INDICATIONS OF THICKER OIL.
